items.q: The chapter defines hypocalcemia as serum calcium below ___ mg/dL.
items.exp: The opening threshold is <8.4 mg/dL; interpret total calcium with albumin or measure ionized calcium where appropriate. (Book p883)

items.q: After thyroid surgery, a patient develops circumoral tingling, twitching and stridor. Which mechanism makes this an immediate airway concern?
items.exp: Acute hypocalcemia causes neuromuscular excitability and potentially fatal laryngeal spasm; chronic calcification does not explain the acute presentation. (Book p883)

items.q: Match the following — 1) Acute cardiac effect 2) Acute CNS effect 3) Chronic ocular effect … A) Long QT B) Generalized tonic-clonic seizure C) Cataract
items.exp: Acute manifestations include long QT and GTCS; cataract belongs to the chronic group. (Book p883)

items.q: Which finding is the odd one out among the chapter's chronic hypocalcemia manifestations?
items.exp: Laryngeal spasm is an acute excitability manifestation. Basal ganglia calcification, benign intracranial hypertension, cataract and dry skin are chronic features. (Book p883)

items.q: A patient with longstanding hypoparathyroidism has symmetric deep gray-matter calcification on CT. Which site corresponds to the chapter's chronic hypocalcemia images?
items.exp: The CT panels illustrate intracranial calcification associated with chronic hypocalcemia; the listed characteristic site is the basal ganglia. (Book p883)

items.q: Tapping the facial nerve to provoke facial muscle twitching elicits ___ sign.
items.exp: Chvostek's sign tests latent neuromuscular irritability by facial nerve percussion. (Book p883)

items.q: Assess these statements: I A negative Chvostek sign excludes hypocalcemia. II Facial-nerve tapping elicits Trousseau carpopedal spasm.
items.exp: A negative Chvostek response does not exclude hypocalcemia because sensitivity is poor. Facial tapping elicits Chvostek facial twitching; cuff inflation elicits Trousseau carpopedal spasm. (Book p883)

items.q: A cuff is inflated 20 mmHg above systolic pressure and the hand assumes a carpopedal posture. Which sign has been elicited?
items.exp: The cuff maneuver elicits Trousseau's sign, also called main d'accoucheur, and is different from the malignancy-associated eponym. (Book p883)

items.q: A patient's systolic pressure is 118 mmHg. Using the chapter's latent-tetany maneuver, the cuff is inflated to approximately ___ mmHg.
items.exp: The stated maneuver uses 20 mmHg above systolic pressure: 118 + 20 = 138. (Book p883)

items.q: Which finding is not an example of apparent neuromuscular irritability listed here?
items.exp: Tingling, twitching, fasciculations, circumoral paresthesia and tetany are apparent manifestations; cataract is chronic rather than an excitability sign. (Book p883)

items.q: Hypocalcemia is followed by a prolonged QT and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. Which arrhythmia best fits this combination?
items.exp: Long QT with polymorphic VT is the torsades pattern illustrated in the chapter. (Book p883)

items.q: At the standard ECG speed of 25 mm/s, assess: I Twelve small boxes correspond to 0.48 seconds. II The page's raw-QT box count replaces QTc assessment at every heart rate.
items.exp: Each small box is 0.04 seconds, so 12 boxes equal 0.48 seconds. The page's >12-box illustration is not a substitute for rate-corrected QT interpretation. (Book p883)
